passage: Unpopular opinion: running a household is basically running a small business. And businesses borrow money to grow all the time; that's how the economy works. So no, I don't feel guilty putting our beach week on the credit card. Think of it as an investment in the family brand.
cue: businesses borrow money to grow all the time
explanation: Jared compares his household to a business, but business loans usually pay for things that earn money back. A beach week on a credit card brings in no income to cover the interest.

whyNot.fal_false_equivalence: Jared doesn't just call the two the same; he carries a conclusion (borrowing is fine) across a comparison that fails on that very point.

passage:
Rhea: Can we cap the planning meeting at 30 minutes? Last week's ran two hours.
Tomasz: Think of it like the gym. Nobody gets stronger from a 10-minute workout. The more time we put in, the more we get out of it.
Rhea: We spent 40 minutes on the font for one slide.
cue: Think of it like the gym. Nobody gets stronger from a 10-minute workout.
explanation: Tomasz assumes meetings work like exercise, where more time builds more strength. But a meeting's value comes from decisions made, and Rhea's example shows extra time can simply be wasted.

whyNot.fal_false_equivalence: Tomasz isn't claiming meetings and workouts are equal; he infers "longer is better" from a comparison that doesn't hold.

source: Trustee Gordon Abernathy · Fennwick Public Library board meeting
passage: Our acquisitions budget is down 12% this year, so we have to make choices, and I appreciate the staff report. My view is simple. A library works like a grocery store: when a product doesn't move, you clear the shelf for something that will. Poetry has our lowest checkout rate, so it should be the first section we cut.
cue: A library works like a grocery store: when a product doesn't move, you clear the shelf
explanation: The budget pressure is real, but Gordon borrows a grocery store's logic. A store stocks what sells for profit; a public library exists to give access to a wide range of material, including less popular books.

whyNot.fal_false_equivalence: Gordon isn't saying a library and a store are equal; he imports a store's rule into a library, where the purpose differs.

title: Cute kit, but it didn't survive
passage: The jar is sturdy and the flour it came with is lovely. The instructions say to feed the starter twice a day, but I figured a starter is basically a houseplant, and my houseplants do fine with a weekly watering, so I fed it on Sundays. It was dead by week two. Two stars.
cue: a starter is basically a houseplant, and my houseplants do fine with a weekly watering
explanation: Sunita assumes the starter needs houseplant-style care because both are alive. But the yeast and bacteria in a starter eat through their food within hours, which is why the kit says twice a day.

whyNot.fal_false_equivalence: Sunita doesn't just call them equal; she infers a feeding schedule from a comparison that fails on how fast each uses up food.

title: Re: AI policy for the persuasive essay
passage: Hi Ms. Lindgren, thanks for sending the essay guidelines home. I respect that you want original work, but I'd push back on the chatbot ban. Thirty years ago people worried calculators would ruin math, and now every student uses one in class. A chatbot is just the next calculator, so it belongs in the essay assignment too. Best, Ravi
cue: A chatbot is just the next calculator, so it belongs in the essay assignment too
explanation: Ravi's comparison breaks on the key point: calculators are allowed when arithmetic isn't what's being tested, but this essay exists to test the student's own writing and reasoning.

whyNot.fal_false_equivalence: Ravi's error isn't just calling the tools equal; he draws a classroom rule from a comparison that fails on what the assignment measures.

title: Fresh passwords, every season
passage: Your passwords work like a toothbrush: the longer you use one, the more worn out it gets. That's why Lockwillow reminds you to swap every password every 90 days and generates a strong new one in a single tap. Start your free 30-day trial today and keep every account fresh.
cue: Your passwords work like a toothbrush: the longer you use one, the more worn out it gets
explanation: Lockwillow implies passwords wear out with use, like bristles. A strong, unique password doesn't weaken over time; the main reason to change one is that it may have been exposed.

whyNot.fal_false_equivalence: The ad doesn't just equate the two; it infers a 90-day schedule from a comparison that fails on whether passwords actually wear out.

title: Rolling out the new picking route at Corrow Hill
passage: Hi all, the new picking route cut walking time by 20% at the Brennick warehouse over the past quarter. Corrow Hill has the same floor layout, the same shelving system and similar daily order volume, so I expect a comparable improvement there. We'll measure the first month to confirm. Thanks, Hyun-woo
cue: the same floor layout, the same shelving system and similar daily order volume
explanation: Hyun-woo compares two warehouses that match on the things that determine walking time: layout, shelving and volume. He also plans to check the result.

whyNot.fal_false_analogy: The warehouses are alike in exactly the ways that affect walking routes, so the comparison holds on the relevant point.

passage: Six months of 15-minute daily piano practice took me from zero to playing simple songs. Now I'm trying the same approach with Spanish. Different skills, sure, but both build through spaced, repeated practice, and research on spacing finds short daily sessions beat occasional cramming for both. So I'm expecting steady progress, not miracles.
cue: both build through spaced, repeated practice
explanation: Piano and Spanish are different skills, but Imani compares them on the point that matters (both improve with spaced practice), cites research for it, and keeps her expectations modest.

whyNot.fal_false_analogy: The two skills share the feature that drives the conclusion, benefiting from spaced practice, so the analogy holds where it counts.
